The `illinois-revealjs` extension gives Quarto's [reveal.js format](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/) an **unofficial** [Illinois-inspired theme](https://marketing.illinois.edu/visual-identity/color).

[![](title-slide-quarto-illinois.png){fig-alt="Title slide of the demo deck in the Illinois theme: the title Overview of the Illinois Revealjs Theme and the subtitle Your Course - Semester YYYY @ Illinois in dark slate, a thin orange rule, the author First Last and the date May 25, 2023, with the slide number 1 / 8 at the top right and the orange block I at the bottom right."}](template.qmd)

The [demo slides](template.qmd) are the `template.qmd` that `quarto use template` gives you, rendered with the current theme ([source](https://github.com/coatless-quarto/illinois-revealjs/blob/main/template.qmd)).

## Installing

To start a new presentation, run this in an empty folder:

```bash
quarto use template coatless-quarto/illinois-revealjs
```

This will install the extension and create an example qmd file that you can use as a starting place for your presentation slides.

To add the theme to a project you already have, run:

```bash
quarto add coatless-quarto/illinois-revealjs
```

## Using

Once the extension is installed, set the `format` inside of the document header to `illinois-revealjs`:

```markdown
---
title: A title
subtitle: A subtitle
format:
  illinois-revealjs: default
author:
  - name: Your Name
    orcid: 0000-0000-0000-0000
    email: alias@email.com
    affiliations: Your Institution
date: last-modified
---
```

Any other [reveal.js feature in Quarto](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/) goes under the `illinois-revealjs` format. For example, the [`chalkboard`](https://quarto.org/docs/presentations/revealjs/presenting.html#chalkboard) feature:

```yaml
format:
  illinois-revealjs:
    chalkboard: true
```

## What the theme sets

The format builds on Quarto's default reveal.js theme and adds:

| Setting | Value |
|---|---|
| Logo | the Illinois block I, at the bottom right of every slide |
| Slide numbers | on |
| Date format | long, such as May 25, 2023 |
| Fonts | Fira Sans for text, Fira Code for code |
| Title slide | title, subtitle, author and date in dark slate, `#1A292C` |
| Rules | a thin orange line, `#EB811B`, under the subtitle and under section titles |
| Links | Illinois orange, `#E84A27` |
| Background | `#FAFAFA` |

The logo, slide numbers and date format can be changed in the document header like any other reveal.js option. The fonts and colors come from the theme's stylesheet, `_extensions/illinois/imtheme.scss`.

## Developer Notes

We created the quarto extension for the revealjs format by using:

```sh
quarto create extension format:revealjs
```

From there, we incorporated a modified version of the [Beamer Metropolis](https://github.com/matze/mtheme) that was ported into a [Quarto theme](https://codeberg.org/pat-s/quarto-metropolis) by [Patrick Schratz](https://pat-s.me/) ([Post](https://pat-s.me/quarto-metropolis-theme/)).

This site lives in `docs/`, which `.quartoignore` keeps out of the files `quarto use template` copies. When it builds, the workflow copies `_extensions/`, `template.qmd` and the title slide image in from the repository root, so the demo always shows the theme as it is on `main`.
